body.en: Quadratic expressions appear frequently on the EST I — in standard, vertex, and factored forms. Knowing how to move between forms and when to use each is a key skill.

Standard: \( ax^2+bx+c \). Vertex: \( a(x-h)^2+k \) with vertex at \( (h,k) \). Factored: \( a(x-r_1)(x-r_2) \) with roots \( r_1, r_2 \). Quadratic formula: \( x=\dfrac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a} \). Discriminant \( \Delta = b^2-4ac \): positive → two real roots, zero → one root, negative → no real roots.

body.en: Solve \( x^2-5x+6=0 \) by factoring. \[ (x-2)(x-3)=0 \implies x=2 \text{ or } x=3. \]

Polynomial operations

To multiply polynomials, distribute each term of the first factor across every term of the second. The key identity \( (a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2 \) shortcuts many EST questions. Dividing a polynomial by a linear factor \( (x-k) \) uses synthetic or long division; the Remainder Theorem states the remainder equals \( f(k) \).

label.en: Worked example — Discriminant & nature of roots

body.en:
Find the values of \(k\) for which \(x^2 + kx + 9 = 0\) has two equal roots.

Equal roots when \(\Delta = 0\): \(k^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0 \Rightarrow k^2 = 36 \Rightarrow k = \pm 6\).

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Quadratics & Polynomials

body.en:
• Vertex Coordinate Signs: In vertex form \(y = a(x - h)^2 + k\), the vertex is \((h, k)\). Notice the minus sign on \(h\): \(y = 2(x + 3)^2 - 5\) has vertex at \((-3, -5)\), NOT \((3, -5)\). From standard form, \(h = -b/(2a)\).
  • Cancelling Variables Loses Roots: In an equation like \(x^2 = 6x\), NEVER divide both sides by \(x\)! Doing so loses the root \(x = 0\). Instead, set to zero: \(x^2 - 6x = 0 \implies x(x - 6) = 0\), yielding both \(x = 0\) and \(x = 6\).
  • Discriminant Root Classifications: \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\). If \(\Delta > 0\), two distinct real solutions (parabola intersects \(x\)-axis twice); if \(\Delta = 0\), exactly one real solution (parabola touches \(x\)-axis at its vertex); if \(\Delta < 0\), no real solutions (parabola lies entirely above or below \(x\)-axis).
  • Sum and Product of Roots (Vieta's Formulas): For \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), root sum is \(r_1 + r_2 = -b/a\) and root product is \(r_1 r_2 = c/a\). This avoids having to solve the equation when the question only asks for the sum or product of solutions.

question.en: The height \(h\) in meters of a projectile launched upward from an initial height of 25 meters after \(t\) seconds is modeled by \(h(t) = -5t^2 + 20t + 25\). (a) At what time \(t\) does the projectile reach its maximum height, and what is this maximum height? (b) After how many seconds does the projectile strike the ground?

solution.en:
(a) Maximum height at vertex: The time at which maximum occurs is the vertex: \[ t = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = -\dfrac{20}{2(-5)} = \dfrac{20}{10} = 2\text{ seconds}. \] Substitute \(t = 2\) to find maximum height: \[ h(2) = -5(2^2) + 20(2) + 25 = -20 + 40 + 25 = 45\text{ meters}. \]

(b) Time to strike the ground: Set \(h(t) = 0\): \[ -5t^2 + 20t + 25 = 0 \implies -5(t^2 - 4t - 5) = 0 \implies (t - 5)(t + 1) = 0. \] Since time cannot be negative, \(t = 5\) seconds.
